title: Find the account, whatever type its id arrived as

blocks.text: The payments service keeps accounts by a 64-bit id. Events reach it through a decoder that turns each message into a `Map<String, Object>`, and old card terminals still check accounts with a 32-bit id of their own. Since the mobile app started sending events, support hears two complaints: some events fail with a `ClassCastException`, and every old terminal reports "account closed" for accounts that are open.
`ownerOf` and `open` already work. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/AccountDirectory.java`:

items: `accountId(event)`: the id in the event's `"accountId"` field, whichever type the decoder chose for it (see the class comment);
`isOpen(terminalAccountId)`: whether the terminal's id names an open account.

cases.says: an event whose id is a Long finds its account's owner, an unknown id finds nobody, and an unknown terminal id is not open
an event whose id the decoder gave as an Integer finds the same owner as the Long would
an id above the int range finds its own account, and an id that differs from an open one only above the low 32 bits finds nobody
a 32-bit id from an old terminal finds the account opened with that id

origin.section: A Wrapper Converts Only to Its Own Primitive: an Integer Is Never a Long

concepts: A cast between reference types converts nothing: it checks the object's class and throws ClassCastException, so (Long) on an Integer fails.
An int boxes to Integer, which never equals a Long, so a Map<Long, …> lookup or Set<Long>.contains with an int finds nothing; Number.longValue() reads either wrapper.
